title: Ekiden Becoming More Popular in UK
paragraphs: A traditional Japanese relay race called ekiden is becoming popular in the UK, with a national race becoming an annual event, and "mini-ekiden" events being held in schools.

Ekiden is a long-distance relay race that's very popular in Japan. Instead of a baton, runners carry and pass on a sash called a tasuki, which represents their shared effort. The sport emphasizes shared responsibility and teamwork rather than the abilities of individual runners.

Ekiden was introduced to the UK by Anna Dingley, 51, who lived and worked in Japan for eight years. There she saw the Hakone Ekiden, and was moved by the runners' efforts and the support they received from local communities who cheered them on the route.
Dingley then organized the first UK Ekiden race in 2024, with 18 teams taking part from the UK, Japan, Canada, Germany and Hong Kong.

The race is now an annual event with separate team categories of "racers" from universities and "runners" from business and community groups, and prizes given to the winning team from each category. Each team has 10 members, and includes men and women.

The third UK Ekiden was held in June 2026 on a 112-kilometer course on the outskirts of London that follows the River Thames, with competitors running along country paths through gates and fields, towns and villages.
In 2024, just three university teams took part in the race. But this year, there were 17 university teams — including Japan's Ritsumeikan University — as well as 18 business and community teams.
The University of Oxford took home first prize in the university category, while a team from insurance firm Marsh came first in the business and community category.

For the last three years, Dingley has also organized "mini-ekiden" events at schools across the UK, encouraging hundreds of school children to learn more about Japanese culture while experiencing the fun of teamwork and friendly competition.
